requirement_text.REQ-062: See handoffs/WF02-REQ062-20260819/step-01-code-designer.json context.requirement_text for the full verbatim requirement description.

task.description: Independently validate lib/letflow/design/req062-sub-process-runtime.md (branch feature/WF02-REQ062-20260819, already checked out) against REQ-062's 8 acceptance criteria (copy them from step-01-code-designer.json's task.acceptance_criteria). Read the design file directly -- do not read step-01-code-designer.json's result.summary as a substitute. Per WF-02 Step 1b: for each AC, confirm a concrete design element exists (no TBD/deferral language), function signatures are fully specified with error cases, error handling shape is stated as tagged tuples not left implicit, cross-module dependencies are listed, and no .ex implementation code bodies are present (signatures/type shapes only). Note: the design's own summary flagged an open question (OQ-1, how a SUB_PROCESS node names which definition to run) as unverified against R-Co source since R-Co is unreachable in this sandbox -- an explicitly-flagged open question is acceptable per WF-02 Step 1's own procedure ("Open questions listed explicitly, not silently resolved"), so do not FAIL solely for that being open; but do check whether the open question actually blocks any of the 8 ACs from having a concrete design element (if it does, that IS a FAIL-worthy gap, not just an open question).
acceptance_criteria: a token entering a SUB_PROCESS node with a declared interface creates exactly one child instance whose initial variable map contains ONLY the declared inputs -- a parent variable not named in inputs is demonstrably absent from the child
a SUB_PROCESS node with no declared interface copies the full parent variable map to the child (EXT-05 behaviour preserved), demonstrated by an explicit test alongside the filtered case

each of the four SPC-01 failure modes has its own test and its own distinct error: the two activation failures leave ZERO child instances created (verified by counting instance rows), and the two completion failures leave the parent's variable map unmodified (no partial merge)

on child completion with a declared interface.outputs, only the named outputs merge into the parent via REQ-049's merge, and a child variable not named in outputs is demonstrably absent from the parent afterwards

the parent token's waiting_child_instance_id is set while the child runs and cleared on completion, and it survives a transition that copies tokens for an unrelated reason -- an explicit regression test for R-Co's GH #428 field-dropping bug
child instance creation is not reachable through REQ-045's public create/1 path, matching R-Co's internal-only createWithParentInheritance shape, confirmed by inspection and stated in the moduledoc
cancelling a parent instance does not cancel its running child, matching R-Co's documented EE-08 behaviour, demonstrated by an explicit test rather than assumed

each of the four SPC-01 failure modes is demonstrated routing into REQ-061's set_instance_error rather than writing its own ERROR transition, confirmed by inspection and by test -- this closes REQ-061's own AC obligation, deferred forward because REQ-062 did not exist when REQ-061 was built

result.summary: Read lib/letflow/design/req062-sub-process-runtime.md directly (not CODE-DESIGNER's summary) and checked all 8 ACs against it, then cross-checked the design's foundational claims about existing code against lib/letflow/engine.ex, lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex, lib/letflow/engine/token.ex, lib/letflow/engine/token_record.ex, lib/letflow/engine/execution_error.ex, lib/letflow/definitions/sub_process_interface.ex, lib/letflow/engine/variable_merge.ex. AC1 (filtered inputs) and AC2 (EXT-05 full-copy fallback) -> §3.2.1 build_child_initial_variables/2 with full @spec, error tuples, and explicit interface==nil vs. interface!=nil branches. AC3 (4 failure modes, zero-child / no-partial-merge) -> §4 summary table + §3.3 (structural 'append_start_multi/6 never called' guarantee) + §3.4 step 2 (merge computed before any Multi step appended). AC4 (output filtering) -> §3.2.2 build_parent_merge_variables/2, same shape as §3.2.1. AC5 (waiting_child_instance_id set/clear/preserve, GH-428 regression) -> §5 + §1.1's struct-update discipline, verified against the real lib/letflow/engine/token.ex (field already exists, confirmed) and lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex's existing struct-update pattern in advance_token/3 etc. AC6 (create/2 has no second entry point) -> §0 + §3.3, verified against the real Letflow.Engine.create/2 (lib/letflow/engine.ex lines 290-303): create_attrs has no parent_instance_id field, matching the design's claim that child creation stays a separate, non-public code path. AC7 (EE-08 no cascade) -> §7, verified word-for-word against the real fetch_and_lock_open_tasks/3 and fetch_and_lock_live_tokens/3 (lib/letflow/engine.ex lines 1782-1850): both filtered strictly on `where t.instance_id == ^instance_id`, confirming the design's 'structurally unreachable' claim is true of the actual code, not just asserted. AC8 (routes through ExecutionError, not a new ERROR transition) -> §4 table + §3.2.3, verified against the real lib/letflow/engine/execution_error.ex: error_type() already reserves :subprocess_interface_violation (line 67) and append_multi/3's real @spec matches the design's usage; also confirmed Letflow.Engine.set_instance_error/2 (engine.ex line 2007) is a real function, matching AC8's own wording. Also verified: Letflow.Engine.Transition's real transition_event()/pending_event() unions (3 and 3 variants respectively, transition.ex lines 96-116) match the design's 'one new variant' framing exactly, and Letflow.Definitions.SubProcessInterface's real parse_interface/2 and validate_schema_shape/2 (sub_process_interface.ex) match the design's 'reused unchanged' claim in shape and arity. No TBD/deferral language found on any of the 8 ACs -- 4 open questions (OQ-1..OQ-4) exist but were checked individually: OQ-1 (SUB_PROCESS definition-reference attribute name) does not leave any of the 8 ACs without a concrete design element -- §3.3's prepare_child_activation/4 states a concrete assumed attribute name/resolution path (node.attributes['definition_name'] via Definitions.get_active_by_name/2) plus a named defensive error code (SUB_PROCESS_DEFINITION_NOT_FOUND) for the case it's wrong, so implementation is not blocked, only flagged for correction if wrong. OQ-2/OQ-3/OQ-4 are genuinely out of this requirement's 8 ACs' scope (registry-schema double-validation, cross-definition recursion depth, cancel-cascade-to-parent) and are correctly left open rather than blocking any AC. Every function signature reviewed carries full @spec-style types with explicit tagged-tuple error shapes ({:ok, _} | {:error, _} throughout); no .ex implementation code bodies present anywhere in the document -- every code-shaped block is a @spec/@type declaration or a table, never a real defp/def body.
